title: River & Redwoods Film Festival

description: The River & Redwoods Film Festival returns to Monte Rio for a special weekend celebrating independent film, creativity, community, and the natural beauty of Northern California. Set among the towering redwoods and along the banks of the Russian River, the festival brings filmmakers, film lovers, artists, and locals together for three unforgettable days of screenings, conversations, live events, and connection. Hosted at the historic Monte Rio Theater and neighboring venues in Monte Rio, California, River & Redwoods showcases narrative films, documentaries, shorts, student films, and emerging voices from the Bay Area and beyond. Whether you're an industry professional, aspiring filmmaker, or simply someone who loves movies under the redwoods, we invite you to spend the weekend with us.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.
source: North Bay Bohemian, Visit Santa Rosa

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.
source: Creative Sonoma, North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

title: JP's Backyard Ultra/Hike
location: Skyline Wilderness Park
description:
Event Description

Join us for JP’s Backyard Ultra, a one-of-a-kind ultramarathon and hike set in the scenic trails of Skyline Wilderness Park in Napa, CA. Now in its fourth and final year, this grassroots event is more than just a race, it’s a celebration of life, resilience, and community.

Born from my personal journey with Stage IV mediastinal paraganglioma, JP’s Backyard Ultra is a fundraiser for the Pheo Para Alliance, a 501\(c\)\(3\) nonprofit \(EIN 26-1510652\) dedicated to empowering patients, families, and medical professionals affected by pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma through education, advocacy, and global support. Learn more at www.pheopara.org.

Whether you’re in it for one loop or ten, come run or hike in solidarity, to honor those facing rare diseases, to challenge yourself, and to stand as part of a growing force for good.

~Jonathan Pascual

The course features a 3.3 mile loop with 550\+ feet of climbing, offering a mix of terrain from steep rocky sections to shaded paths. Scroll down for map below.

Participants can choose anywhere from 1 to 10 loops.

Runners and hikers alike start at the same time every hour going clockwise on the even hours and counterclockwise on the odd hours. So it doesn’t matter if you finish your loop fast or slow because everyone starts again at the same time in the next hour. Those attempting 10 loops should pace themselves for a final race on the 10th loop making 33.3 miles. You can do as many or as few loops as you wish however.

Timed Event: 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM. Please arrive by 0730 for course description, announcement of run prize categories & fundraising prizes.

Aid Station: Main camp has various caloric options and drinks with water only at the bridge and mile 2.3.

Food & Beverages: Provided, including lunch for participants and volunteers.

Cupless Event: Bring your own water bottle or hydration pack. HYDRAPAK, our Sustainable Racing Partner will provide limited 300 Limited Edition HydraPak Graphic SpeedCups & 8 SpeedFill Pitchers for use at aid stations.

Awards:Medals to all registered hikers and runners.Medal & wine \(non-alcoholic option for under 21\) for top three male and female finishers of the 2, 4, 6, 8 loops.Medal, wine, and trophy for the fastest 10th loop goes to the top three male and female finishers and special Vinerunner 4th place trophy.Medal, wine, and trophy for the fastest cumulative time for 10 loops goes to the top three male and female finishers.

Raffle Prizes: buy tickets on day of event to win raffle baskets, gift certificates, and other special prizes. Proceeds benefit the Pheo Para Alliance.

Silent Wine Auction: place your bids on exceptional wines generously donated by local Napa Valley wineries, starting at an unbeatable buy-now price. Proceeds benefit the Pheo Para Alliance.

Registration “Fee”: Donation LinkJP’s Backyard Ultra has always been a free event. Suggested donation to register starts at $30.Participants get a medal, a variety of snacks and drinks at the aid station, and lunch.To streamline registration, we are using runsignup.com. 100% of suggested starting donation of $30 goes directly to the Pheo Para Alliance. The processing fee of 6% per $1 of transaction \(cart\). This fee is charged per transaction, not per individual participant, meaning that if a user registers multiple people to a single cart, the $1 fee is only charged once, lowering the overall cost per person.If you cannot attend or want to donate beyond the suggested amount, consider giving an additional donation at the donation link.

title: Apple U-Pick at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
location: Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
**Our popular Apple U-Pick Experiences return for a second year!**

Experience the magic of harvest season at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, where you can hand-select the most flavorful Honeycrisp or Fuji apples straight from our certified organic orchard.

Timed entries from 8:30am. Last orchard entry at 11:30am.

Admission: $8 for adults, $3 for children. Registration required.

U-Pick apples: $4 per pound.

**Apple U-Pick FAQs** 

Do I need a reservation? 

Yes! Please reserve your time slot on our reservation site. Reservations help us ensure everyone has a wonderful experience without overcrowding.  

Can I show up without a reservation? 

We require reservations to maintain our capacity limits and ensure everyone enjoys their visit to the fullest.  

Can I cancel my reservation?  

Absolutely! You can cancel your reservation up to 48 hours before your scheduled time by calling us at 707-823-3100. Please note that cancellations made less than 48 hours in advance will result in forfeiture of the entrance fee. 

Can I bring my dog?  

Dogs are not permitted in the orchard, with the exception of service animals. This policy helps ensure the safety and comfort of all our visitors. 

Can I bring a stroller into the orchard?  

For safety reasons, strollers aren't allowed in the orchard, but you're welcome to leave yours at the check-in area where it will be safe and waiting for you!  

I require mobility accommodations. Can I still pick apples in the orchard?  

Yes. Please call us on 707-823-3110 once you’re made a reservation and we can provide suitable transportation into our orchard.

Why is there an entrance fee?  

The entrance fee helps us maintain our beautiful orchard and keep our experienced staff on hand to ensure everyone has a safe and enjoyable experience. 

How much are the apples?  

Our delicious U-pick apples are $4.00 per pound.  

What variety of apples will we be harvesting?  

You'll be picking either Honeycrisp or Fuji apples (depending on seasonal availability).  

Can I harvest heirloom apples?  

While heirloom apples aren't available for U-pick, we offer many wonderful heirloom varieties for purchase in our Farm Shop.  

Are your apples organic?  

Yes, all our apples are organically grown and certified annually by Oregon Tilth!

title: Family Garden & Farm Program

description:
Vallejo Project is excited to announce the launch of its Family Garden & Farm Program, a hands-on learning experience designed for families with children ages 0–5. The program invites parents and caregivers to join young children in exploring gardening, nature, healthy food, and farm animal experiences at Unity Garden in Vallejo.

The Family Garden & Farm Program creates opportunities for families to learn and grow together through interactive activities that build early childhood development, environmental awareness, and healthy lifestyle habits.

Through weekly family-centered experiences, children and caregivers will have the opportunity to:

 Plant flowers, fruits, and vegetables  Harvest fresh produce from the garden  Meet and care for friendly farm animals  Feed chickens and goats  Explore nature and outdoor spaces  Learn about healthy eating and where food comes from  Develop early learning, communication, and life skills

“Children learn best when they can touch, explore, create, and connect with the world around them,” said Adjoa McDonald, Founder of Vallejo Project. “This program brings families together in the garden and farm environment to build confidence, strengthen relationships, and create positive memories around food, nature, and community.”

Participating families will receive hands-on activities, garden starter resources, fresh produce opportunities, and family learning experiences designed to support children’s growth and curiosity.

The program will also measure its impact through family surveys and staff observations, tracking outcomes related to:

Caregiver confidence in gardening and teaching children about plants

Children’s connection to nature and animals

Healthy eating habits

Outdoor learning and exploration

Family engagement and community connection

The Family Garden & Farm Program is open to families with children under age five. Space is limited.

title: Heart & Mind Equine Rescue: Self-Compassion with Horses
location: Heart and Mind Equine
description:
Offered by Heart & Mind Equine Rescue. Meet our rescued therapy horses, explore our volunteer program, and learn about holistic horse keeping and equine-assisted services \(e.g., therapy, coaching, leadership, and team building with horses\). No experience is necessary. All are welcome, including both horse and mental health professionals.

What would it feel like to offer yourself the same kindness and care you so freely give to others?

Join Alane Freund and the Heart & Mind Equine herd for Self-Compassion with Horses, a 90-minute experiential session designed to help you slow down, become present, and reconnect with yourself.

Through mindfulness, reflection, and guided experiences with the horses, we’ll explore self-compassion, self-awareness, grounding, and authentic connection.

Horses naturally invite us into the present moment. Their sensitivity and responsiveness can help us notice what we’re feeling, soften self-criticism, and practice meeting ourselves with greater kindness and curiosity.

What to Expect

• Guided experiences with the horses • Mindfulness and grounding • Reflection and self-compassion practices • Connection in a supportive, welcoming environment

No horse experience is necessary. All activities are ground-based.

Come as you are and spend a morning practicing a little more kindness toward yourself.

Space is limited. Reserve your place today.

Curious about Equine Assisted Services? Horse Rescue Class is not therapy, but it is an opportunity to get a “taste” of our work with our equine colleagues since we use some of the same tools and exercises in both settings. Come out and meet the herd \(both humans and horses\) connected with Heart & Mind Equine.

Each month, the class is centered on a theme such as holistic horse keeping, equine-assisted learning, understanding herd dynamics, holistic horse care and training, and how these all relate to our human journey.

Nature or horse lovers, high achievers living with stress, spiritual seekers, highly sensitive people, mental health providers, parents, and teachers might especially benefit from this class as well as horse owners/riders who hope to improve their relationships with their equine partners. \(Though this work is great for dogs as well, your dogs are not welcome at our horse rescue due to liability and distraction concerns.\) Newcomers and novices are most welcome. Service dogs do not usually do well at the barn, but please email to discuss.

Come and experience the magic of working with horses firsthand. Get ready to roll up your sleeves, get your hands dirty, and connect with these majestic creatures. Whether you're a seasoned equestrian or just starting out, there's something for everyone at our Speaking Horse classes. Don't miss out on this exciting chance to bond with horses and fellow horse lovers. We can't wait to see you there!

Children 9 and older are welcome with adult participation and supervision \(and legal guardian signed liability release\). Youth 15 and older may attend alone with a signed parental permission form. We meet in a pasture which has uneven ground and slippery gravel. For these reasons, we offer limited accommodation for participants with mobility challenges. \(We are able to offer some in-place, chair-based experiences, as well as onsite parking, so we invite those with challenges to reach out to learn more. Please call to RSVP 415-203-6600, first come, first served.\)

Holistic horse keeping methods and perspectives form the primary vision for our rescue. This class is a fundraiser for the nonprofit horse rescue, so please donate what you can, either here, by VenMo, or at the class. Note that Eventbrite will charge you a processing fee. Directions and liability paperwork are sent upon registration. This is a volunteer orientation as well. It is an opportunity to meet our herd, both horses and humans, and find out if you might like to get involved. All registration fees are donations that support the rescue herd.

Register for directions to the barn.

title: Jack London State Historic Park WILD Trail Challenge
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
On Saturdays from Sept. 5 to Oct. 3, Jack London State Historic Park’s WILD Trail Challenge returns for a third year.  This series of five hikes covers every trail in the park for a total of 39.5 miles.  The hikes increase in duration and/or difficulty each week.

Participants can sign up for individual hikes or do them all.

The price for each hike is $15.  The park entry fee of $15 per vehicle is waived for these hikes.  Those who sign up for all five hikes before Sept. 5 save 20 percent and pay only $60.

Hike \# 1 – Historic Trails

September 5, 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.  

A great way to warm up. This hike explores the historic sites and trails of the park. Navigate both sides of the park to discover Jack London’s Beauty Ranch, London Lake, and the Wolf House ruins.

Easy – moderate hike \(approximately 4.5 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 2 – Ancient Redwood

September 12, 9 a.m.-1 p.m.   

Meander through the redwoods and sunny oak woodlands of the park’s three Bridge Trails \(Upper, Lower, and Fallen\). The journey leads to the majestic ancient redwood, fondly known as the Grandmother Tree.

Moderate hike \(approximately 6 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 3 – Historic Orchard

September 19, 9 a.m.-1:30 p.m.   

Start Location: Note that this hike does not begin at Jack London State Historic Park

Sonoma Developmental Center

Arnold Dr, Eldridge, CA 95431

Stroll along the blue shores of Fern Lake before reaching the Historic Orchard. Learn about the history of the land and the fascinating fruit-bearing crops that thrive there.

Moderate – Difficult hike \(approximately 7 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 4 – Ridge

September 26, 9 a.m-3:30 p.m.   

Details: Hikers will gain elevation and an appreciation for the diverse habitats found within the park. They’ll also traverse part of the ever-growing Bay Area Ridge Trail.

Difficult hike \(approximately 12 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 5 – Summit 

October 3, 9 a.m.-2:30 p.m.     

A trek to the park summit is the perfect way to complete the WILD Trail Challenges.  Climb Sonoma Mountain to enjoy stunning views, celebrate with fellow hikers, and become a WILD One.

Difficult hike \(approximately 10 miles roundtrip\)

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a September 2026 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.

location: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Cuentos con Ritmo (Stories with Rhythm)
location: Children's Museum of Sonoma County
description:
Cuentos con Ritmo \(Stories with Rhythm\)



Cuentos con Ritmo | Cuentos \* Música \* Movimiento 

Presentado por Colors of Spanish 

Cuentos con Ritmo es una oportunidad única semanal para niños de 1 a 5 años y sus familias, el cual aporta alegría, comprensión y aprecio por la lengua española a toda la comunidad. Durante Cuentos con Ritmo, los pequeños visitantes y sus familias participan de forma lúdica en historias interactivas con música y movimiento fortaleciendo nuestra diversa comunidad y entusiasmo por la lengua meta. 

Cuentos con Ritmo es presentado por Guadalupe Tausch en colaboración con la organización que fundó, Colors of Spanish. Originaria del estado de Guanajuato en México, tiene una maestría en español con énfasis en la adquisición de una segunda lengua para la primera infancia y continúa sus estudios enfocada en la primera infancia especializándose en la adquisición de idiomas a través de la música/movimiento. Colors of Spanish ofrece talleres para profesores, bibliotecarios y cuidadores y organiza programas de cuentos en español con música y movimiento en escuelas, bibliotecas y museos locales. www.colorsofspanish.org 

Cuentos con Ritmo | Cuentos \* Música \* Movimiento 

Presented by Colors of Spanish 

Cuentos con Ritmo \(Stories with Rhythm\) is a weekly one-of-a-kind opportunity for children ages 1-5 and their families that brings joy, understanding and appreciation for the Spanish language to Spanish- and English-speaking speakers alike. During Cuentos con Ritmo, young visitors and their families playfully engage in interactive stories with music and movement that build community and an excitement for language! 

Cuentos con Ritmo is presented by Guadalupe Tausch in collaboration with the organization she founded, Colors of Spanish. Originally from the state of Guanajuato in México, she has a master’s degree in Spanish with emphasis in second language acquisition for early childhood and continues her study of childhood and music/movement trainings. Colors of Spanish provides workshops for teachers, librarians and caregivers and hosts Spanish story time with music & movement programs at local schools, libraries, and museums. www.colorsofspanish.org 

Designed for kids 1-5, families, and siblings. 

 

Generously sponsored by RCU and the SABA Foundation.

title: Digital Detox: The Wisdom of Rest, Balance, and Ease
location: Spirit Rock Meditation Center
description:
with Nikki Mirghafori

In a world of constant demands, endless to-do lists, and attention pulled in every direction, our nervous systems can tighten, leaving us drained and overwhelmed. This daylong offers a welcoming invitation to pause, breathe, and rediscover the wisdom of rest, restoration, spaciousness, and mindful presence. Guided meditations, embodied awareness, silence, and time in nature help settle the body, steady the mind, and renew energy and attention, gently returning us to what matters most. Practices of lovingkindness and equanimity nourish the heart, reminding us that we are always enough. Equanimity does not mean not caring—it means caring deeply with wisdom and balance. Through mindfulness, we learn to meet life with greater clarity and kindness rather than reactivity. Rest here is not selfish: it replenishes us for the benefit of ourselves and others. Join us to cultivate a more spacious and easeful way of being, and step into more freedom.

Join artist and educator, Valerie Seaberg for a two-day immersive lantern-building workshop inspired by Día de los Muertos, ancestral remembrance, and joy of creating in community. Together we will create illuminated lantern sculptures that honor loved ones, celebrate lineage from all cultures and traditions, and welcome the deepening beauty of fall and winter. Using willow, bamboo, reed, paper, and other sustainable materials, participants will learn how to build expressive sculptural lanterns from the inside out. Participants are encouraged to bring ideas, sketches, photographs, symbols, or meaningful inspiration connected to ancestors, memory, nature, or personal vision. title: Honoring the Sacred Feminine
location: Tayu House, Sebastopol
description:
A Day of Reflection and Exploration For Men and Women
Conducted by Ginny Matthews & Regina Sara Ryan 
The Sacred Feminine is an energetic life force that is present (at least in seed-form) in all of us, whatever our gender. Disconnected from this aspect of our essential nature, we lose touch with the full promise and possibility of Life. This gathering is designed to encourage us all (men & women) to recognize and renew our dedication to this Sacred Feminine power of creation: the power that supports life in all forms, nurtures health and happiness in ourselves and others, and forgives, blesses and eases pain and suffering wherever it is found. The responsibility, privilege and joy of honoring and renewing this Sacred Feminine Principle in our world today is a necessity…and now more than ever. 
Ginny and Regina will lead us in a few meaningful rituals, and encourage us to create our own that we can integrate into daily life. They will offer some guidance in meditation practice, and allow time to “write from the heart,” as a way to keep our connection to heart alive. Music, movement and chant will allow us to celebrate what we know, what we are, and make an offering to others.
You can use this day to rest and inspire yourself in the company of other pilgrims on a sacred path. A chance to put away cellphones, computers, family and business work, to deepen your connection with nature, and to focus on what feeds your soul.
If interested in participating, please contact Ginny Matthews at myosho@sonic.net so we may prepare the space and expect you.

In this special four-week workshop, participants will explore the unique art of reduction relief printmaking. Acclaimed guest artist, Tomoko Murakami, will demonstrate how to create multi-color prints from a single linoleum block. The main idea is to gradually carve away parts of the block and print each new layer of color, with each layer building on the previous one. The course covers the entire process, from designing and planning, to carving techniques, inking, registration, and printing with both hand and printing press methods. Participants will learn to explore the possibilities of color mixing and layering, enabling students to achieve intricate designs and a wide range of visual effects. You will gain an understanding of the materials, processes, and innovations involved in this unique form of relief print printing!All levels are welcome, including continuing linocut students. Please note: This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver the carving tool. Participants should feel comfortable standing, and using tools with sharp blades and edges.

title: On Site Compost and Biochar Demonstration
location: Sonoma Garden Park
description:
Please join us for the first in a series of composting workshops taught by Bobby Nicholson of Compost Depot with the Sonoma Ecology Center (SEC) and Sonoma Biochar Initiative (SBI). The workshops are funded by Zero Waste Sonoma (ZWS) and free to the public. The workshop series will continue with five on site compost workshops throughout Sonoma county. 

Let's get dirty! The workshop will provide practical guidelines and accessible soil science to build a healthy composting program on location with available resources and using a scalable model. Raymond Baltar of SBI will introduce the basics and science of biochar, including use of the flame cap kiln, and demonstrate the integration of biochar into a compost program.This will be a handson learning opportunity for agricultural producers of all sizes, and at the end of the workshop, attendees will have the resources and know-how to build a composting program on-site. The workshops will be bilingual, taught in English and Spanish.

Le invitamos a participar en el primero de una serie de talleres sobre compostaje impartidos por Bobby Nicholson, de Compost Depot, en colaboración con el Sonoma Ecology Center (SEC) y la Sonoma Biochar Initiative (SBI). Estos talleres cuentan con el financiamiento de Zero Waste Sonoma (ZWS) y son gratuitos para el público.

¡Manos a la obra! El taller ofrecerá pautas prácticas y nociones accesibles de ciencia del suelo para establecer un programa de compostaje saludable en el propio lugar de trabajo, utilizando recursos disponibles y un modelo escalable. Raymond Baltar, de la SBI, presentará los fundamentos y la ciencia del biocarbón —incluyendo el uso del horno de tipo "flame cap" kiln— y demostrará cómo integrar este material en un programa de compostaje. 

Será una oportunidad de aprendizaje práctico para agricultores, productores agrícolas, encargados de jardines o invernaderos y paisajistas de cualquier escala. Al finalizar el taller, los asistentes contarán con los recursos y los conocimientos necesarios para implementar un programa de compostaje en sus propias instalaciones. Los talleres serán bilingües (impartidos en inglés y español).

Fecha: Sábado, 26 de septiembre de 2026; de 10:00 a. m. a 1:00 p. m.

Lugar: Sonoma Garden Park, 19996 7th St E, Sonoma, CA 95476

Dirigido a: Agricultores, productores agrícolas, encargados de jardines o invernaderos y paisajísticas del condado de Sonoma.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

“Piper has the kind of voice that lulls men to their doom. It’s soft and sweet 

when it wants to be, scared and vulnerable a moment later, then ripping through 

you like a razor… Piper commands songs utterly.”

Jeremy Loome, The Edmondton Sun, Canada

One listen will tell you why in her homeland Anni Piper is known as the First Lady of Blues. 

Not only is she a sultry vocalist, but an insightful composer, accomplished bass player and 

show stopping performer. Born and raised in Australia, her passion for blues was ignited by 

the sound of Stevie Ray Vaughan. Piper has called the United States home since 2014.

‘Blow Up Doll’ \(Sugar Daddy Records 2020\) is the latest release for Piper and the second on 

her own label. Already an internationally acclaimed recording artist, her latest achievement 

is becoming a semi-finalist in the 2019 International Songwriting Competition.

Picking up a bass guitar at age 14, Piper completed a Bachelor of Contemporary Music 

degree at 19 years of age. Finding it difficult to resume her performing career following the 

birth of her son, Piper recorded her debut album ‘Jailbait’ in 2004. The all original album was 

meant to be a good quality demo and wasn’t intended for commercial release.

To Piper’s surprise, she was immediately signed to Black Market Music, Australia’s most 

prestigious blues label and began touring throughout the country. The ‘Jailbait’ album won 

multiple awards including Best New Talent at the Australian Blues Music Awards, the ABC 

Radio National ‘Fresh Air’ contest, and 2nd place at the Australian National Songwriting 

Contest.

Her subsequent releases saw her placed as a finalist in the Australian Blues Music Awards 

\(Best Female Vocal\), UK Songwriting Contest, Australian Performing Rights Association 

Professional Development Awards, MusicOz awards and semi-finalist in the International 

Blues Challenge. Piper has earned a reputation as a songwriter of distinction, her work 

having a blues sensibility while still addressing the issues of today.

In 2008 Piper signed with Blues Leaf Records USA \(Janiva Magness, Albert Castiglia\) and 

released ‘Two’s Company’, a compilation of her earlier releases. The album reached \# 21 on 

the Living Blues chart even though Piper had yet to tour the USA. She quickly made up for 

lost time and has performed in 45 American states and Canada. Piper has performed to 

packed houses at premier venues such as the House of Blues and BB King’s. She has earned 

critical acclaim from publications including Blues Revue and Blues Matters \(UK\)

title: Healdsburg Internation Short Film Festival 2026
location: The Raven Performing Arts Theater
description:
This three-day festival runs from September 25th through September 27th. Organized in collaboration with the **Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA**), HISFF 2026 coincides with HCA’s **Festival of the Arts**, creating a vibrant, art-filled weekend.

HISFF 2026 kicks off with an Opening Night Soirée, a lively red-carpet arrival and photo op at the Raven, and an exquisite collection of mixed genre short films. Festivities continue with multiple screening sessions, a Saturday night party at **The Rooftop at the Harmon Guest House**, and a filmmaker breakfast, culminating in an awards ceremony on Sunday night.

Our panel of notable judges from the entertainment industry makes the HISFF an attraction for new and veteran filmmakers alike — people like **Ed Begley, Jr., Laraine Newman, Billy Ray, Tom Waits**, and so many more. Several judges are attending the festival this year, including writer Billy Ray (*The Hunger Games* and the soon-to-be released *The Hunger Games: Sunrise On the Reaping* ), who will make a book-signing appearance at the Raven on Saturday, September 26th (Time TBD).

Visit our booth at the Healdsburg Festival of the Arts on Saturday, September 26th, from 10 am to 6 pm on Center Street in front of HCA (just steps away from the Raven). The street will be lined with booths featuring fine arts, crafts, jewelry, poetry, live music, food trucks, and more!

Copperfield’s is organizing a free-admission book-signing event with screenwriter (and festival jurist) Billy Ray at the Raven from 11:00 am, also on Saturday, September 26th. Books will be available for purchase and signing, but it’s best to order your copy ahead of time from Copperfield’s.

**All Access Pass: $175. Includes:**

\- Red-Carpet arrival and photo op begins at 6 pm at the Raven.

\- Opening Night Kick-Off Screening Block, 7:00 pm.

\- Opening Night Kick-Off Soirée, 8:30 pm at Portalupi Wines.

\- Every screening session, including the filmmaker Q&A sessions.

title: Memoir Writing Workshop for Women: Crafting Your Life Story
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Transform Your Memories into Meaningful Narrative
A Writing Retreat in Beautiful West County
Ready to tell your story? Your memories are waiting to become literature.
Discover the power of your personal story and learn to craft it with authenticity, depth, and literary grace.
Workshop Overview
Join us for an immersive memoir writing experience designed to help you uncover, shape, and share the stories that have defined your life. Whether you're a complete beginner or have been writing for years, this workshop will provide you with the tools and confidence to transform your memories into compelling prose.
What You will Learn:
Memory Mining Techniques
: Discover how to access and explore your most meaningful experiences
Narrative Structure
: Master the art of organizing your life events into engaging storylines
Voice & Perspective
: Develop your unique authorial voice and choose the right point of view
Scene Construction
: Learn to craft vivid, cinematic scenes that bring your memories to life
Truth vs. Accuracy
: Navigate the ethical and creative considerations of memoir writing
Character Development
: Portray yourself and others with complexity and compassion
Revision Strategies
: Polish your work through effective editing techniques
Workshop fee is $147, $127 for OCA members. This workshop is limited to 8 participants and will be held in the OCA Studio.
Register
Workshop Format
Duration
: One Saturday ( 4 hours total).
Class Size
: Limited to 8 participants for personalized attention
Format
: Interactive sessions combining instruction, writing exercises, and peer feedback
Materials Provided
: Writing prompts, handouts, and recommended reading list
Who Should Attend
Aspiring memoir writers at any experience level
Anyone interested in preserving family history
Writers looking to explore personal narrative
Individuals seeking therapeutic writing experiences
Those curious about the memoir genre
What to Bring
Notebook and writing materials
Open mind and willingness to share (in a supportive environment)
No previous writing experience necessary
Led By
Alaura O’Dell MFA, an experienced memoir author and writing instructor, will guide you through each step of the creative process with warmth, expertise, and encouragement. Alaura has guest lectured at Santa Rosa Junior College, Marin College and Sonoma State University. O’Dell is currently working on a memoir, which has attracted an international publisher. For over 30 years she has lead women’s workshops and classes, including with her company, Sacred Journeys for Women, facilitating retreats to sacred sites around the world.

title: The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout [OPTION 2]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
Publisher's description: Artie Dam is living a double life. He spends his days teaching history to eleventh graders, expanding their young minds, correcting their casual cruelties, and lending a kind word to those who need it most. He goes to holiday parties with his wife of three decades, makes small talk with neighbors, and, on weekends, takes his sailboat out on the beautiful Massachusetts Bay. He is, by all appearances, present and alive. But inside, Artie is plagued by feelings of isolation. He looks out at a world gone mad—at himself and the people around him—and turns a question over and over in his mind: How is it that we know so little about one another, even those closest to us?

And then, one day, Artie learns that life has been keeping a secret from him, one that threatens to upend his entire world. Once he learns it, he is forced to chart a new course, to reconsider the relationships he holds most dear—and to make peace with the mysteries at the heart of our existence.

Elizabeth Strout, as we have come to expect, delivers a moving exploration of the human condition—one that brims with compassion for each and every one of her indelible characters. With exquisite prose and profound insight, *The Things We Never Say* takes one man’s fears and loneliness and makes them universal. And in the same breath, captures the abiding love that sustains and holds us all.

"I haven't enjoyed a Strout book this much in years. Strout takes you inside Artie, gradually revealing pieces of his past and his relationships. Despite the premise, much of the book is upbeat, and when it isn't, we're rooting for Artie." - Joan

"More wonderful characters and interesting narrative from Strout. Highly recommend." - Dave

"I too, am a fan of *The Things We Never Say.* I was immediately drawn into this novel. Can't wait!"

title: Sullivan Rutherford Estate's Annual Event of Artistry & Excellence
location: Sullivan Rutherford Estate
description:
Join us on Saturday, September 26th from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. for an afternoon celebrating excellence, creativity, and authenticity at the intersection of wine, art, and hospitality at Sullivan Rutherford Estate.

Set against the backdrop of harvest in Rutherford, Napa Valley, guests will gather around a grand table for a thoughtfully curated experience featuring exceptional wines from Sullivan Rutherford Estate Winemaker Jeff Cole, extraordinarily inventive cuisine from one of the Napa Valley’s most renowned chefs and meaningful conversation. James Beard Award-winning Chef Rogelio Garcia will present a four-course culinary journey inspired by the season's finest ingredients, thoughtfully crafted in dialogue with the artistic expressions of both ceramicist Adán Paredes and Winemaker Jeff Cole. Live music will provide the soundtrack to an afternoon designed to foster connection, celebrate creativity and a shared appreciation for craftsmanship, artistry, and excellence.

Throughout the event, guests will have the opportunity to engage with world-renowned ceramic artist Adán Paredes, whose work reflects a lifelong dedication to craftsmanship and creative expression. Joining him will be Sullivan Rutherford Estate’s Winemaker Jeff Cole, whose own artistry takes shape in the vineyard and cellar in order to produce the most iconic Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon expressions of Rutherford. Throughout the afternoon, guests will enjoy a curated selection of wines, including a limited preview of an unreleased bottling of our Family Reserve available exclusively for this celebration.

Harvest is a season that reminds us that the most meaningful experiences are rarely created alone. They emerge through patience, collaboration, dedication, perseverance and a shared commitment to excellence. This celebration brings together three distinct forms of artistry: winemaking, creative cuisine, and one-of-a-kind visual expressions for an unforgettable afternoon among friends. Tickets are $425 per guest, or $550 for two tickets for Founder’s Members.

He will be joined by Healdsburg's own Melissa and Sean McGaughey of Quail & Condor and Troubadour Bread & Bistro, who are known for crafting excellent French cuisine with Sonoma County ingredients.  Quail & Condor’s baked goods are highly acclaimed—as a 2025 James Beard Finalist and ranked by The New York Times as one of the best bakeries in America. 

Your cornucopia of farm-to-table cuisine will be perfectly paired with sparkling wine from Hafner Vineyard—a three-generation Healdsburg Winery that has mastered the art of French wines. You’ll also be treated to refreshing Aperol Spritz, and Champagne. 

Gather your friends to enjoy this special evening with bubbles, a playful game of bocce, and delicious food from some of the Sonoma County’s best chefs. Don’t miss your chance to attend this lively, fun-filled experience! 

Our sincere gratitude to the Fry Family and Hafner Vineyard for making this experience possible.

title: Culture in Choreography - Asian American Pioneers In Dance
location: Jarvis Conservatory
description:
*Culture In Choreography*, a new ongoing cinematic series at The Jarvis Conservatory, explores diverse perspectives and experiences in dance.

The inaugural screening features two documentaries by acclaimed filmmaker Jennifer Lin (*Beethoven in Berlin*), offering complementary perspectives on the Asian American experience in ballet. Together, the films journey from a study of the past to a benchmark for the future, celebrating Asian American pioneers in dance and the artists who are carrying their legacy forward.

Through these compelling stories, *Culture In Choreography* invites audiences to reflect on the people, histories, and cultural perspectives that continue to shape the world of dance.

**TEN TIMES BETTER** unveils the remarkable story of an 88-year-old Chinese blackjack dealer in Las Vegas whose forgotten past reveals an extraordinary place in ballet history.

**ABOUT FACE: DISRUPTING BALLET** is a 60-minute documentary following two New York City dancers as they challenge the elite ballet world to confront and eliminate racial stereotypes embedded in beloved classics such as *The Nutcracker* and *La Bayadère*.

Together, the films serve as bookends to the story of Asians in ballet—one uncovering a hidden chapter from the past, the other documenting artists shaping a more inclusive future. Both films were directed by acclaimed filmmaker, Jennifer Lin (Beethoven In Beijing).

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Ink & Rhythm
location: Petaluma Museum
description:
A Live Performance Celebrating Creativity, Memory & Cultural Connection

Experience an extraordinary collaboration between acclaimed Chinese American artist Jun Jun and internationally celebrated Zimbabwean musician Piwai, as painting and music unfold together in a live performance exploring creativity, memory, and cultural connection.

Throughout the evening, Jun Jun will create expressive paintings in real time while Piwai responds through song, mbira, and rhythm, weaving together two artistic traditions in an improvisational dialogue that transcends language. Together, they invite audiences to experience how art can carry memory, celebrate identity, and build bridges across cultures.

Following the performance, meet the artists, explore the exhibition, and enjoy authentic Zimbabwean cuisine provided by the Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California.

title: Full Moon Hike

description:

title: California Indian Museum and Cultural Center 30th Anniversary Gala
location: Balletto Vineyards
description:
For 30 years, the California Indian Museum and Cultural Center \(CIMCC\) has been a vital and unique resource advancing understanding of California Indian history, cultures, and contemporary leadership. On Saturday, September 26, 2026, at 5:00 pm, CIMCC will celebrate three decades of impact with an anniversary gala —an inspiring evening honoring Indigenous excellence, celebrating community, and looking toward the next generation of Native leadership.

The event will showcase the richness, resilience, and creativity of Native communities while raising critical funds to advance CIMCC’s work to preserve and share cultural knowledge, strengthen intergenerational connections, empower Native youth and families, and nurture Indigenous leadership for generations to come.

Guests will be treated to an unforgettable Native traditional food dinner prepared by award-winning Chef Justin Pioche, a 2023 James Beard Award Finalist for Best Chef of the Southwest \(AZ, NM, NV, OK\) and Food Network Chopped Champion. The evening will also feature a cocktail reception, silent auction, inspiring stories of CIMCC’s impact, and vibrant Native entertainment—all set against the beautiful backdrop of Balletto Vineyards in Santa Rosa.

description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. Join The Floathouse for a magical evening paddle on the Petaluma River—Petaluma’s Longest Park—timed to catch the full moon rising over the wetlands just south of downtown. As twilight fades, we’ll head out together in Hobie pedal kayaks for a relaxed, guided glide that turns nighttime into playtime.

This is a social, feel-good outdoor experience designed for anyone looking for something a little different to do after dark—part nature, part adventure, part pure vibe.

$60 per person includes everything: • Hobie pedal kayak • PFD and safety lights • Experienced local guide • A memorable, moonlit river experience

✨ Easy. Playful. Peaceful. Spend your evening under the full moon—on the water.

Join us for line dancing lessons from Grapevine Dance! Plus live music from Dustin Saylor & The Stowaways.

About Dustin Saylor:

Dustin Saylor, a Northern California-born country singer-songwriter, has made a name for himself as the #1 Country/Folk artist in the San Francisco Bay Area. His musical journey began in childhood, first at the piano and later as a guitarist and singer for his high school youth group and local church. Despite early challenges, including a devastating American Idol rejection in 2009, Saylor had a transformative moment on his long drive home, realizing that true success required full commitment. Embracing his calling, he quit bartending, pursued a music degree at Sonoma State University, and became a full-time musician. Over the years, he has performed alongside artists like Tyler Rich, Chase Rice, and Daughtry, with his sound often compared to Thomas Rhett and Chris Stapleton. His songwriting is deeply personal, shaped by his early experiences of adoption and the contrasting struggles and joys of his life. Through his music, Saylor seeks to inspire, heal, and create a space where people can connect beyond labels. Committed to his craft, he remains "all in," determined to sing and play music for the rest of his life.

title: Dear Evan Hansen
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description:
Poignant, raw, and of-the-moment, Dear Evan Hansen pulls back the curtain on the profound desire for human connection in the digital age, offering an empathetic look at the alienation of young people navigating modern social pressures.

The story follows Evan, a high school senior struggling with severe social anxiety who writes motivational letters to himself as a therapeutic exercise. When a troubled classmate dies by suicide with one of Evan’s letters in his pocket, the boy's grieving parents mistakenly believe Evan was his secret best friend. Desperate to comfort them, Evan plays along, spiraling into a web of fabricated emails and internet fame before he must ultimately face the truth.

Powered by a critically acclaimed pop-rock score and the sweeping anthems, Dear Even Hansen is a powerful reminder that we are never truly alone. Spreckels is proud to present the North Bay premiere of this six-time Tony Award winning musical!

location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Introduction to Indonesian Batik: Wax, Color & Storytelling

Introduction to Indonesian Batik: Wax, Color & Storytelling Sunday, September 27th, 2026 10:00am-1:00pm $95.00 + $25.00 Materials Fee = $120 Attendance Price Discover the beauty of Indonesian batik in this beginner-friendly, hands-on textile workshop. Batik is a traditional wax-resist art form from Indonesia, where wax is used to create patterns and protect areas of fabric before color is added.Students will begin with a short introduction to the cultural background and storytelling traditions of Indonesian batik. Then, step by step, they will create their own small batik artwork on fabric using a traditional canting tool, hot wax, and fabric dyes. Participants may work from a simple provided design or develop their own motif with guidance.This class is designed to be creative, relaxing, and approachable for complete beginners as well as textile artists who want to explore a new process. All materials and tools will be provided, and students will leave with their own handmade batik piece to take home.No previous drawing or batik experience is required. Because hot wax is used, students will receive clear safety guidance throughout the workshop.About the Teacher: Theresia Debby Iriani is an Indonesian batik artist, clothing designer, and founder of Oedel Batik, a modern batik clothing line she has been developing since 2018. Since 2023, Theresia has also opened hands-on batik classes for guests visiting Bali, and has led batik painting workshops for international visitors, families, children, schools, and corporate groups in Bali. Theresia’s classes introduce students to the cultural background of Indonesian batik while guiding them through a hands-on process using traditional wax-resist techniques, canting tools, and fabric dyes. Theresia has experience adapting batik workshops for beginners, small creative groups, and larger events. Theresia’s teaching style is warm, step-by-step, and focused on helping each participant feel comfortable exploring their own design and creativity. Click here to see more of Theresia’s work on her Instagram!

title: River & Redwoods Film Festival

description: The River & Redwoods Film Festival returns to Monte Rio for a special weekend celebrating independent film, creativity, community, and the natural beauty of Northern California. Set among the towering redwoods and along the banks of the Russian River, the festival brings filmmakers, film lovers, artists, and locals together for three unforgettable days of screenings, conversations, live events, and connection. Hosted at the historic Monte Rio Theater and neighboring venues in Monte Rio, California, River & Redwoods showcases narrative films, documentaries, shorts, student films, and emerging voices from the Bay Area and beyond. More than just a film festival, River & Redwoods is about gathering in a beautiful small-town setting to experience great storytelling together. Expect filmmaker Q&As, outdoor gatherings, music, local food and drink, and the laid-back creative spirit of Sonoma County. Whether you're an industry professional, aspiring filmmaker, or simply someone who loves movies under the redwoods, we invite you to spend the weekend with us.

title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting
description:
Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

Find a meeting: https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Slow down and float into a quieter rhythm with SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River at The Floathouse Petaluma. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this peaceful on-the-water yoga experience feels worlds away from the bustle—set in the calm, protected turning basin where the river naturally invites you to relax.

This all-levels, 90-minute session welcomes everyone, from first-time paddle boarders and yoga newcomers to experienced practitioners. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board \(knees are always welcome\), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. Once settled, you’re free to move, stretch, rest, or simply be—guided by expert instruction and supported by the shared energy of the group. Evening sessions and morning sessions allow YOU to choose the vibe that suits you best.

All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards that are wider and longer than a yoga mat, designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water.

Perfect for locals and Bay Area visitors alike, SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River offers a rare chance to experience downtown Petaluma from the water—peaceful, playful, and deeply restorative.

It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Soul Motion®: Body Prayer every Sunday in person

BODY PRAYER IS A FACILITATED EVENT DEVOTED TO INQUIRY INTO EMBODIED CONSCIOUSNESS THROUGH MOVEMENT. 
This class is offered every Sunday morning, and led by Zuza Engler or another teacher. It is usually attended by a vibrant & diverse bunch of welcoming and friendly people, some of whom have practiced Soul Motion® for years, while some ~ never before. 
What to expect 
Guidance and structure are part of every week’s class as we travel across the four landscapes of Soul Motion®:
Dance Infinite (prayer space)
Dance Community (ensemble)
Dance Communion (duet)
Dance Intimate (solo) 
Practices, structures, and points of view are offered to facilitate the journey. Participants are invited to travel across all landscapes, not just their favorite one: dancing by oneself, in duet, in ensemble with several people and eventually the whole room, or witnessing in stillness the beauty of another’s or of everyone’s dance. 
Body Prayer offers a place to be safely uncomfortable as we experiment with ourselves and with each other in our awkward and magnificent dance at the edge of possibility. 
No experience necessary! Everyone welcome!

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Nothing To See Here - Jason Perry
location: Mare Island Art Studios
description:
"Nothing To See Here" is a critical, yet playful examination of the UFO phenomenon that is hinged on the dynamic between serious scientific inquiry and fringe science.

With a mixed media approach that combines drawing, collage, and painting, Jason Perry seeks to entice the viewer into the work through familiar visual iconography, bold colors, expressive marks, and textures. Once there, the viewer is offered a deeper layer of meaning to consider. Perry calls into question the blurred narratives, misinformation, and potential truths surrounding the UFO topic.

At its core, "Nothing To See Here" invites us to look a little closer at our beliefs, our relationship to the strange, the unexplained, and our enduring fascination with what might be out there.

description:
**Soul Meets Keys: Marcus & Devin Live**

Join us for No Cell Sundays with Marcus & Devin, a duo that transforms Sunday afternoons into something extraordinary.

Marcus Urani is one of Northern California's most celebrated pianists and keyboardists. Educated in musical theory and an original member of Groundation, Marcus has toured the world and spent 25+ years composing, arranging, producing, and playing with countless musical acts. With mastery across nearly all genres, Marcus creates rich musical landscapes that captivate from the first note.

Paired with vocalist and lyricist Devin Ruddick's emotive and soaring vocals, this duo delivers a one-two punch that captivates without intrusion—adding melodic bliss as they cover a catalog of meaningful artists spanning seven decades.

**What's No Cell Sundays?**

It's simple: disconnect from your devices, reconnect with great wine, live music, and the people around you. *Check your phone with us at the door and receive a complimentary tasting.* Bring a blanket, grab a glass, and spend your Sunday the way it was meant to be spent.

title: Healdsburg Internation Short Film Festival 2026
location: The Raven Performing Arts Theater
description:
This three-day festival runs from September 25th through September 27th. Organized in collaboration with the **Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA**), HISFF 2026 coincides with HCA’s **Festival of the Arts**, creating a vibrant, art-filled weekend.

HISFF 2026 kicks off with an Opening Night Soirée, a lively red-carpet arrival and photo op at the Raven, and an exquisite collection of mixed genre short films. Festivities continue with multiple screening sessions, a Saturday night party at **The Rooftop at the Harmon Guest House**, and a filmmaker breakfast, culminating in an awards ceremony on Sunday night.

Our panel of notable judges from the entertainment industry makes the HISFF an attraction for new and veteran filmmakers alike — people like **Ed Begley, Jr., Laraine Newman, Billy Ray, Tom Waits**, and so many more. Several judges are attending the festival this year, including writer Billy Ray (*The Hunger Games* and the soon-to-be released *The Hunger Games: Sunrise On the Reaping* ), who will make a book-signing appearance at the Raven on Saturday, September 26th (Time TBD).

Visit our booth at the Healdsburg Festival of the Arts on Saturday, September 26th, from 10 am to 6 pm on Center Street in front of HCA (just steps away from the Raven). The street will be lined with booths featuring fine arts, crafts, jewelry, poetry, live music, food trucks, and more!

Copperfield’s is organizing a free-admission book-signing event with screenwriter (and festival jurist) Billy Ray at the Raven from 11:00 am, also on Saturday, September 26th. Books will be available for purchase and signing, but it’s best to order your copy ahead of time from Copperfield’s.

**All Access Pass: $175. Includes:**

\- Red-Carpet arrival and photo op begins at 6 pm at the Raven.

\- Opening Night Kick-Off Screening Block, 7:00 pm.

\- Opening Night Kick-Off Soirée, 8:30 pm at Portalupi Wines.

\- Saturday Night Sweet & Uncorked Social at the beautiful Harmon House Rooftop, 8:15 pm.

\- Every screening session, including the filmmaker Q&A sessions.

title: Dear Evan Hansen
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description:
Poignant, raw, and of-the-moment, Dear Evan Hansen pulls back the curtain on the profound desire for human connection in the digital age, offering an empathetic look at the alienation of young people navigating modern social pressures.

The story follows Evan, a high school senior struggling with severe social anxiety who writes motivational letters to himself as a therapeutic exercise. When a troubled classmate dies by suicide with one of Evan’s letters in his pocket, the boy's grieving parents mistakenly believe Evan was his secret best friend. Desperate to comfort them, Evan plays along, spiraling into a web of fabricated emails and internet fame before he must ultimately face the truth.

Powered by a critically acclaimed pop-rock score and the sweeping anthems, Dear Even Hansen is a powerful reminder that we are never truly alone. Spreckels is proud to present the North Bay premiere of this six-time Tony Award winning musical!

Established in 2017, the Alpha Rhythm Kings have created quite a stir with music fans, crafting an exciting "King Size California sound" that No Depression magazine calls "the badge of authenticity." The "swaggering" \(Washington Post\) ensemble, led by Rob Dehlinger's "exhilarating" trumpet and "magnetic" vocals \(Jazz Corner\), has become a favorite with audiences all over the globe, from Idaho to Indiana, and Beverly Hills to Budapest. In 2025, Rob Dehlinger and the Alpha Rhythm Kings were invited to Osaka, Japan, to represent the United States as performers at the World Expo. Sonoma Sundays are free and open to all, thanks to the generous support of the Sonoma Community Center, The Dawn Redwoods Trust, and the McNeely Family Foundation. Pack your picnic, bring your dancing shoes, and meet us on the Plaza!

Acorn’s 27-member vocal ensemble, directed by Sarah Dupre, will be joined by violin, cello, and piano on this piece, and on multiple other pieces. The concert includes a variety of other original compositions, including by Sarah Dupre, Robin Eschner (AMP co-directors), and Moira Smiley.

title: Acorn MusEcology Project: The Earth Says
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Acorn MusEcology Project is proud to present the Northern California premiere of Alex Berko's
Sacred Place
, an immersive exploration of ecological spirituality set to the words of Wendell Berry, John Muir, William Stafford, and Rabindranath Tagore. Acorn's 27-voice ensemble will be joined by violin, cello, and piano to offer up this song cycle of reverential texts within a richly-layered soundscape. Additional original music by co-directors Sarah Dupre and Robin Eschner includes a new setting of poetry by the late Steve Fowler, co-founder of the Sebastopol Peace Garden, soil ecologist, and community builder. Acorn composer Chris Smith will usher listeners into the alchemical mysteries of human composting. Joni Mitchell, Moira Smiley, and other master songsmiths round out the program. With Acorn's signature approach to melding rich vocal harmony with the values of deep ecology, this concert will invite reflection on our place and purpose on the Earth, and on the wild intelligence speaking to us from beneath our feet.
"The earth says have a place; be what that place requires; hear the sound the birds imply and see as deep as ridges go behind each other...Listening, I think that’s what the earth says."
– William Stafford.

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html
