title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker
location: Petaluma Arts Center
description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.

The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
location: Christ Church United Methodist
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Slow Meditative Birding Journey
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
Do you enjoy a slow walk in a valley, breezes, wildflowers, the sounds of songbirds, the taste of a Douglas Fir needle or a California Bay leaf, the aroma of Tarweed, or watching wild turkeys and California Quail hunt for seeds and insects in the grass? Join Certified California Naturalists and Sugarloaf docents for this series of meandering explorations. Each month (weather permitting) we will explore one or two of our three accessible trails-- the Creekside Trail, the Nature Trail, and the Meadow trail. Suitable for all levels and a range of mobility, these Sunday afternoon adventures will accommodate people using walkers or wheelchairs, young children, parents with babies in strollers, as well as those who just enjoy slow walks in nature that stimulate the five senses. 

Our October outing will focus on meditative birding. We will start off by sitting quietly for 10 minutes with Merlin app recording in 3 different locations, followed by about 10 minutes of discussion of the birds we heard, using Cornell to confirm their calls and songs before moving onto the next sitting spot. We will also saunter (while looking for birds) between the locations for a total distance of ~1.3 miles on an accessible trail. Birding by ear lends itself to meditation because it works best when you sit silently and listening closely (i.e., if Merlin *hears* something you did not, it reminds you that your mind has wandered). 

Tickets are $5 for adults and free for children under 18 years of age. All minors must be accompanied by parent or legal guardian. **Tickets day-of, on site will be $10 and might not be available.** Meet at the White Barn parking lot.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: California Native Creations Art Show
location: Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center
description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 1

This class focuses on the simple delight of mixing color with water, brushing it on paper, and watching what happens as it moves and dries. You will learn easy ways to create paintings that are all about color and the sometimes unpredictable nature of water.

No drawing skills are needed.

In this class we will explore the basic principles of watercolor painting. Learn or refresh your understanding of brush handling, brush care and setting up, the benefits of “good paper”, watercolor lights and darks, flat and graded washes, wet-on-wet techniques such as charging, wet-on-dry techniques such as glazing, color wheel, color theory, color mixing, and more. Simple applications of these techniques invite you to experiment and play.

This class is designed for adults 18+ (exceptions made for very motivated teens, please email to discuss)

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 2

This next series will build on what we learned in Part 1, quickly refreshing some techniques and then applying them in our paintings. We will create more complex landscape paintings, skies and seascapes; wet-into-wet and wet-into-dry nature studies in a few different ways, and we will venture further into painting from our imaginations. We will explore abstraction and non-representational styles, where we don't look at something and try to paint it, but instead work intuitively with colors and shapes and let the paintings emerge and evolve from there. You don't have to know where you're going, enjoy the journey and see where it takes you!

This class is designed for adults 18+

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
location: 1st Street Gallery @ WTRSHD
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present *“Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,”* a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 *voyages to the* Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, *Yurok/Kashaya Pomo*, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled *Mind Prison,*

·         Digital artist Nicolas (Nico) Vargas, *Kashia Band of Pomo Indians*, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, *Kashia Band of Pomo Indians*; Angelica Smith, *Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria*; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, *Kashia Band of Pomo Indians*; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, *Big Valley Pomo Tribe*.

title: Garden Tours Guided by Osmosis Founder + Lead Gardener (10/21)
description:
Experience the Osmosis Meditation Garden with Its Founder on Wednesday, October 21st 

Join the founder and lead gardener of Osmosis for a guided journey through our landmark meditation garden — an intimate event limited to just 12 guests. 

Discover the artistry and intention behind one of Osmosis’s most beloved spaces as we explore the principles of Japanese garden design: the carefully chosen plantings, distinctive pruning styles, and deliberate placement of stone. At the heart of the garden lies its foundation — an ancient Zen story told entirely through stone arrangements. 

This is a rare opportunity to see the garden through the eyes of its creator and to understand how every element was thoughtfully composed to create a sanctuary for reflection and renewal.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two *ofrendas* in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS

EXHIBIT DATES – September 28 – October 25, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma County artist, Laura Roney, unveils Aspirations, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration, Aspiration and Awe splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, Aspiring to Vote, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, Aspiring for 26.2, captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s Intentional Chaos, a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in Patterns of Memory multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. \(707\) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    www.upstairsart gallery.net 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Give 'Em the Axe! Ladies Night at the Range in Santa Rosa
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us for an axe-throwing session to blow off some steam. I'm super excited to be able to offer a ladies' Axe-throwing night in Santa Rosa. If you've ever had a curiosity about this fun activity, this is your chance to find out more!

We have reserved a group spot with the indoor range on a Wednesday night. It will consist of an introductory lesson, and then we all get to practice taking turns. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment and targets are provided by them, and we will probably get about 1 to 2 hours to enjoy ourselves.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy).

There are 10 spots available, guests welcome. The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Daima Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

Closed-toed shoes are recommended.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

title: Yoga Vinyasa & Pranayama
description:
Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga
**Yoga Vinyasa Krama - Thursdays 9-10:30am**
**Songbird Community Healing Center Cotati**
**RSVP ONLY**
Physical Health, Conditioning, Pranic Flow, Vital Energy, Mental Focus & Stillness - through intelligent architecture with the metaphysics of deep conscious breathing & slow motion, yogic breathwork, mantra/sound/vibration, mudra, subtle & contemplative practices.
Yoga Vinyasa Krama is a comprehensive hatha-raja yogic system for purification, developing concentration, neuromuscular fitness and conditioning, refining & mastering the breath, awakening subtle energy and stilling the mind. Based on deep breathing & the subtle movement of prana directed into the cartilage tissue, sinuous musculature, internal organs, nerve pathways and nadis. It has over 700 intelligently sequenced slow, conscious breath powered with precision movement variations with pause (vinyasas), exploring many aesthetic variations of each posture to correctly establish the main asanas while the mind merges with the breath.
Includes the energetics of drishti, pratikriyas, bandha, vaseth, mudra, mantra, surya & ding namaskar with breath & mantra, cleansing kriyas, Himalayan pranayama including including ujjayi variations, heating & cooling breaths, solar, lunar & soli-lunar nadi shuddhi practices, pranava & samantraka pranayama, pratyahara, subtle & contemplative practices in 12 kramas (sequences).
The whole process gradually transforms the body and mind, releasing old patterns of physical and mental tension and dysfunctional patterns of movement, providing tonic, energetic and psychophysiological effects.
This system is presented from the teachings **Srivatsa Ramaswami** learned through his over 33 years of one on one study with **Sri Krishnamacharya** and teachings from a similar **Himalayan method**.
This ongoing class will explore the entire system of 12 Kramas with each class focusing on a particular krama or vinyasas from different kramas & pranayama & dharana practices.
Please practice on an empty stomach. Morning beverage ok but please take it 30min or more before class.
***Certain injuries & health issues may be contraindicated Please contact me if you have a concern***
Knowledge of Ujjayi Breathing recommended

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

title: Paint an Oil Portrait
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
CLASS: OIL PAINTING FOR ALL LEVELS
$380 includes all materials—paint, mediums, and oil-primed linen canvas

This is a five week course.

Register for class: https://www.parrcreate.com/page/711614 https://www.parrcreate.com/page/711614

 https://www.parrcreate.com/page/711614
Oil painting doesn’t have to be intimidating! In just four weeks, students will paint a portrait in the indirect style, starting with a grey value study, building up with layers, and finishing with powerful details. The final result always surprises people: just by following basic rules, anyone can create a beautiful oil portrait that glows. Even abstract painters can benefit from learning these techniques.

Knowing how oil painting works gives us more confidence to develop our own authentic creative voice. As Maggie says, “You gotta learn the rules to break the rules.”

Maggie Parr started her career working as a show designer at Walt Disney Imagineering, where she designed theme park attractions around the world. She also expanded into book illustration, murals, portraits, comics, and eventually, writing books and scripts for television. She also developed her own painting practice. To that end, she studied with master teachers like Steve Huston, Jeremy Lipking, and Joseph Q. Daily. She got an MFA and taught at the college level, then developed her own teaching methods for private and group study. Today, Maggie maintains a thriving business creating custom art and designs for corporations, individuals, and non-profits.

She teaches other artists to utilize classical rendering techniques so they can confidently break the rules in the service of their own work. And she coaches creatives in search of deeper authenticity, healing, and self-actualization.


Forms of contact below.

http://www.maggieparr.com http://www.maggieparr.com

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

Dinner & A Show with MIRACLE MULE 
Miracle Mule is a rocking, hoof-stomping, tail-swishing band from Marin County, California. Some folks might describe our music as good-time Americana, others might say it’s down-home country with a heavy dose of Louisiana hot sauce. We prefer to just call it “swampy tonk.” However you describe it, it’s fun and energetic, irresistibly danceable, with rich harmonies and solid song writing. We play at most of the more prestigious venues in the north bay, as well as a host of wineries, festivals and concert series. We have a loyal following, but there’s always room for more. Check us out soon. Dance, Laugh, Bray.

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

Let's make beautiful art together!

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
*• "*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. The class will use two different techniques and Jan will explain how to press flowers and which flowers hold their color best. It is a creative experience!


To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

*A note to all students: Please park on in the East facing parking lot while attending classes. We greatly appreciate it. Thank you.

title: Patrick Ball: Celtic Harp & Story
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Step into the enchanting world of
Patrick Ball
, one of the premier Celtic harp players in the world and a captivating storyteller whose performances weave music, legend, wit, and wonder into an unforgettable experience.
With the crystalline beauty of the Celtic harp as his musical voice, Ball brings ancient Irish tales and timeless melodies vividly to life, transporting audiences to a world of heroes and dreamers, mystery and mischief, heartbreak and humor. His masterful playing and gift for storytelling create an evening that is at once intimate, magical, and deeply human.
Join us at Occidental Center for the Arts for a spellbinding journey through the music and stories of Ireland with a true master of the tradition.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM, refreshments available. Art gallery open during event.
Get Tickets
About Patrick Ball:
Whether in the stronghold of a Galway chieftain in the years before history began or yesterday in the snug corner of a pub in Dublin, the Irish have always delighted in storytelling. Their passion for eloquence and wordplay, their deep devotion to their mythical past, their ability to find joy and humor in a dark world, and their belief that the supernatural world could appear between one breath and the next made their stories and the telling of them unrivaled in the world of the oral tradition.
And always, amidst the storytelling, there was music. Jigs, reels and haunting airs graced the spaces between the tales. And first among Irish instruments, and the most honored, was the legendary Celtic harp. With its crystalline, bell-like voice and lavish resonance, it would soothe its listeners and lead them deeper into the realms of the imagination.
In
Celtic Harp and Story
Patrick Ball rekindles the fire and wonder of an evening of Irish storytelling. For in telling the marvelous old tales of wit and enchantment, and in playing the ancient, brass-strung harp of Ireland, he not only carries on two of the richest traditions of Celtic culture, but blends them in concert to create “a warm and magical performance.”
“An American master of the Irish instrument, a peripatetic modern day bard, combining tale-telling, history and music into a seamless compound that reaches all ages and types of listeners.”—San Francisco Chronicle
“It’s rare that we will feature a performer on our fine performances season for two consecutive years, but then Patrick is a rare artist ... The audience was entranced by his harp playing, amused by his storytelling. Patrick is a grand man who puts on a great show.”—APAP Report / Humboldt State University
“The SRO audience loved Mr. Ball's performance, asking when we will be bringing him back. Ball was a delight to work with, very professional, and he is superb at captivating an audience.”—APAP Report / Arizona State University
“Patrick Ball conjured some Druid magic ... weaving words and music into a spellbinding program.”—The Blade, Toledo, OH

title: Yoga Vinyasa Krama - Talasana Krama & Pranayama
description:
Nataraja School of Traditional Yoga
All Classes RSVP Only at least 24hrs prior
[[breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com)]([mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com](http://mailto:breathprayeryoga@protonmail.com/)), 707-235-1413
\**For All Classes - Certain injuries & health issues may be contraindicated - Please contact me if you have a concern*
**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**
**Mondays 9-10:30am - Songbird Cotati - RSVP**
**$25, Discounted Class Passes & Sliding Scale Available**
Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).

description:
Poetry Lives! October 27th

  
    
      
      from $0.00
    
  

Every Fourth Tuesday: October 27th 6:00-7:00pm: Spoken Word Workshop 7:15-8:30pm: Open Mic Open to All$5/10/15/20 Sliding Scale for Workshop Join us for an evening of spoken word poetry here at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts! Students of all walks of life, abilities, and experience writing poetry, or spoken word poetry, are encouraged to join. Students will engage in a freewrite, poetry reading, discussion, and structured writing with a voluntary shareout. After the one hour workshop, Poetry Lives! will act as an Open Mic night open to all to read their completed, or previously completed, poems. To register for the Open Mic only, please select Open Mic Only below! All workshop registrations include registration to the open mic as well. Poetry Lives! is a monthly poetry workshop and open mic series that aims to create a space for anyone and everyone to come, learn more about poetic craft, and share their poetry. The event starts with a facilitated hour-long workshop dedicated to learning craft elements, discovering new poets, and generating new work. Once the workshop concludes, we will hold a hosted open mic for anyone who wishes to share. It is not mandatory to participate in the workshop to be a part of the open mic or vice versa. This event is all ages, but that doesn't necessarily mean family-friendly, as poets are known to cover mature and adult topics from time to time. About the Poet: Jordan Ranft (He/Him) is a writer and therapist from Northern California. He has been nominated for a Pushcart and Best of the Net. His poetry has been published or is forthcoming in Boulevard Magazine, Frontier Poetry, Poetry Online, Bear Review, Iron Horse Literary Review, and elsewhere. His first chapbook, Said the Worms, was published in June 2023 by Wrong Publishing. He is currently working on a second chapbook and full-length collection. title: Readers' Theatre
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
2nd & 4th Tuesdays, 2-4 pm in the OCA Lobby
Interested in learning, sharing and reading short plays? Readers Theatre is a fun opportunity to express yourself.
Readers Theatre participants read scripts adapted from literature, while the ‘audience’ pictures the action by hearing the script being read aloud. It requires no sets, costumes, props, or memorized lines. Instead of acting literature as in a play, the performer’s goal is to read a script aloud effectively, enabling the audience to visualize the action. Performers bring the text alive by using voice, facial expressions, and some gestures. $15 participation fee, $10 for OCA members.
Alternating READER’S CHOICE nights: Can be play, poetry, story, essay, your own writing, OR ??????
For more information, email
Joan Ambrosini,
coordinator .

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Schnucks Wine Dinner with Jeff Bundschu // SOLD OUT //
description:
Schnucks Wine Dinner with Jeff Bundschu
We invite you to join Jeff Bundschu at Schnucks Des Peres in St. Louis MO on Wednesday October 28th from 6-9pm for a special wine dinner. It will be a culinary experience you won’t want to miss, delicately paired with exceptional wines and their friendly staff.

FROM THE HOST
Join us for an exclusive five-course culinary journey featuring the exceptional cool-climate estate wines of Gundlach Bundschu, Sonoma’s oldest continuously family-owned winery. The evening features sixth-generation vintner and special guest Jeff Bundschu, who will share his personal stories, deep-rooted passion, and distinctively vibrant approach to California winemaking. As each meticulously paired course unfolds, you will gain firsthand insight into the unique terroir of their historic Rhinefarm estate, their sustainable wine-growing philosophies, and the meticulous crafting process that has defined the Bundschu family legacy for nearly 170 years.

MENU
Greeter: Gundlach Bundschu 2025 Gewurztraminer | Gundlach Bundschu 2025 Sauvignon Blanc } Goat Cheese Tart with Asian Pear and Star Fruit | Gundlach Bundschu 2024 Chardonnay } Seared Scallops with Green Apple Beurre Blanc | GunBun Pinot Noir 2022 } Smoked Turkey Roulade with Wild Rice | Gundlach Bundschu Mountain Cuvee 2023 } Cocoa Rubbed Rack of Lamb with Plum Reduction, Sweet Potato Puree and Haricot Vert | Gundlach Bundschu 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon } Basque Chocolate Cheesecake with Blackberries

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Thursdays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 11:30am - 1:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with the instructor for details.


This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcome.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 2]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
\*• "\*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

Instructor: Magdalena Bogart
Date: Monday, November 2nd
Time: 1:00PM-4:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
Fee: $45.00


In my ongoing Gel-Printing & Collage workshop I want to offer you the opportunity to collage with your handmade papers, starting with an easy project progressing each class to a more challenging one.

I will demonstrate techniques for making papers with and without the Gel-Plate. We will create a collection of cohesive
papers. The best of them you will use for your collage projects.

description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

title: Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class) — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class)

  
    
      
        
          $165.00
        
      
    
  

Introduction to Drawing Portraits from Photos November 4th, 11th, and 18th 6:00-9:00pm $150.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $165.00 Age Restricted to 18+ About this class: In this three week course, students will learn and practice observational skills and fundamental drawing techniques while learning the basics of drawing portraits from photographs. Drawing human faces requires the same basic drawing skills that one employs for any subject - observing proportion, flattening shapes, and utilizing line or value to convey volume. But the conceptual weight of human faces tends to intimidate artists. When drawing any subject, the hardest skill is simply learning to see, a skill that anyone can be taught, practice, and hone. This course will focus on the practice of looking, and discovering strategies to find objectivity when rendering portraits. This class is for anyone who wants to practice and advance their drawing skills - beginners, those who haven’t practiced in years, or any artists who just want to learn new techniques and practice their skills with consistent feedback and guidance. Through demonstration, practice, and reflective discussion, this class will explore the foundations of rendering human expression with classical drawing techniques in a low pressure environment. Observational drawing gives all artists a foundation of practical knowledge and skills that infinitely expands the possibilities of what one can create. If your ideas feel limited by your drawing skills, if you feel frustrated or stuck in your painting practice, or if you simply want to start drawing and are looking for a place to start, this is the class for you.About the Instructor: Hannah Day received her BA in Visual Arts with an emphasis on drawing and printmaking from University of San Diego, then attended University of Hawaii at Manoa to receive her MFA in printmaking. Hannah’s etchings have been internationally shown and collected, but her art practice also includes paper cutting, graphite, and watercolor. She has taught all ages in many mediums. These days, Hannah primarily teaches watercolor, observational drawing, and paper cutting. You can view her work at www.hannahdrawstrees.com

title: Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November

  
    
      
        
          $10.00
        
      
    
  

Friday, November 6, 2026; 1:30 – 4:00pmDue to limited capacity, we are asking for a suggested donation of $10 to the Sebastopol Center for the Arts to confirm your attendance. Bring a copy of your receipt at check-in to Painting/Drawing Studio adjacent to Ceramics Studio. Additional donations are welcome at the time of the class to cover rental and expenses for the peace project. Join us for a monthly, heart-centered gathering where we come together to create Jizo guardians out of clay—symbols of compassion, protection, and peace. Rooted in the Buddhist tradition and echoed across many cultures, Jizo figures traditionally honor children and all who have passed, those in transition, and those in distress.This ongoing project is dedicated to remembering those lost to war, with a special focus now on the approximately 19,000 children who have perished in Israel and Gaza in recent years. Through the simple, meditative act of working with clay, we create benevolent beings that will become part of public exhibits and peace sites, offering spaces for reflection, mourning, and hope. Our gatherings conclude with a gentle ritual to honor the lives of these children.Located in the Painting & Drawing Room. The gathering is open to ages 12 - adult, and no prior clay experience is necessary—all clay and basic materials are supplied. Registration is required to participate.Donations are welcome to help cover materials and expenses. More than a class, this is a shared space of warmth and care—an opportunity to tend to our own hearts while taking part in love in action.

description:
Occidental Center for the Arts presents Electric Tumbleweed! One of Sonoma County's finest bands returns for our listening and dancing pleasure.
Tickets are $20/$15 for OCA members. Doors open at 7:30 PM. No dogs. Refreshments available. Free parking.
Get Tickets
Electric Tumbleweed is a psychedelic outlaw country group based in Sonoma County, California. Founded in 2019 by members rooted in bluegrass, country, and psychedelic rock, the music is a hard driving mixture of twangy guitar and psychedelic noise, held together by a steady rhythm section with the cry of pedal steel layered in between it all. Electric Tumbleweed has maintained steady momentum in the Northern California music scene; backing David Nelson (New Riders of the Purple Sage) on multiple occasions; most notably at the Mystic Theater with guest Mark Karan (Ratdog) for a sold out performance. Electric Tumbleweed performed regularly at Phil Lesh’s Terrapin Crossroads as a solo group as well as with Scott Law, Barry Sless (Phil Lesh and Friends) and Dave Zirbel (Sammy Hagar Band) are regular pedal steel players in the group. The band has been invited to play multiple festivals and events including The String Cheese Incident’s Hog Farm Hideaway, Ain’t Necessarily Dead Fest (backing David Nelson). We aim to keep our goals high, and to perform high quality music; focusing on writing and arranging new songs, and booking future tour dates. We are excited to release our debut full-length album in October 2021, which features Sam Bush (New Grass Revival), Barry Sless (Phil Lesh & Friends), and Lester and Dylan Chambers (The Chambers Brothers). The album features the artwork of Stanley Mouse/Jennae Bennett and was engineered and mastered by Grammy winning Oz Fritz (Tom Waits).

title: Returning to the First Mark with Catherine Cruz - November 7th — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Returning to the First Mark with Catherine Cruz - November 7th

  
    
      
        
          $130.00
        
      
    
  

Returning to the First Mark November 7th, 2026 - 11:00am-3:00pm Attendance Price: $130.00 Ages 16+In this new workshop we will explore drawing and abstract mark making through play, curiosity, and child-like wonder.Before we learned to write words, we communicated through marks. As children, we drew with curiosity, freedom, and a sense of play - without worrying about getting it "right” and without fear of getting our hands dirty.  We played in the dirt and we made things.  This workshop invites you to reconnect with that creative spirit through abstract mark making and intuitive drawing.Using a variety of drawing tools and materials, we'll explore line, texture, rhythm, and gesture as a personal visual language. Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, you'll discover how letting go of expectations can open the door to greater creativity and self-expression.Whether you're an experienced artist or simply curious about abstract drawing, you'll leave with new techniques, greater confidence, and a renewed sense of creative freedom. No drawing experience is necessary - just a willingness to explore. Returning to the first mark means:→ reconnecting with curiosity→ slowing down and truly seeing→ discovering the language within ordinary things→ responding intuitively→ building something personal through lines and marksParticipant must bring the following:Note: There is no need to buy expensive materials, please consider what you already have.  If you’re missing something, let the instructor know, Sebastopol Center for the Arts has a minimal amount of these supplies available to borrow.Apron or clothing you don't mind getting paint onBlack gesso or black acrylic paintSpray bottle with water Acrylic paint: two or three earthy colors such as burnt umber, raw sienna, or yellow ochre.  If you don’t have these specific colors, no need to purchase them, just bring whatever you haveA small container, like a glass jar, to pour the gesso inA variety of paint brushes (3 to 5) from very thin to thickA container for waterDifferent types of paper to draw on, from small to large sheets.  Examples: recycled book pages, copy paper, drawing pad, newsprint, brown paper bags, vintage papers with or without illustrations but nothing too dark or too busy. Two black pens or markers with different tipsGlue stickScissorsPaper towelsThe class will begin with a talk and a demonstration, so please plan to arrive early to allow time to settle in.A short lunch break will be held from 12:30 to 1:00 PM. Kindly bring your own lunch and beverage.About the instructor: Catherine Cruz is a French-American artist whose work is informed by textures and patterns created by the passing of time and the effects of the natural elements on the built environment. She holds a Bachelor of Science in interior design and she worked in the field of architectural design and green building certification for over 25 years. She has taught collage and mixed media workshops in the Bay Area and in France since 2019, and this is her fifth year at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts. Her studio is located in Sebastopol and she participates in Art Trails Open Studios. You may contact Catherine at beyouartstudio@gmail.com. Check out Catherine’s other classes here: https://wwws.sebarts.org/visual-arts-classes.

title: Dublinesque Album Release Party
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Don't miss this special evening where we’ll take a musical trip to Dublin with some of the Bay Area’s finest musicians and singers! Eamonn Flynn, Darcy Noonan, Hector Bragado and Felim Egan will dazzle us with their traditional and original "Dublinesque" harmonies. OCA favorites through and through, we're just delighted to bring back this spirited, talented group.
Tickets are $25, $20 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM. Refreshments available, art gallery open during intermission.
Get Tickets
EAMONN FLYNN & DUBLINESQUE
Eamonn Flynn forges his own brand of Irish soul. The Dublin-born singer-songwriter/pianist got his start with The Commitments, a hit film about an Irish soul band, and has since worked with American blues and R&B stars Elvin Bishop, Maria Muldaur, Evelyn Champagne King, Michael Franti & Spearhead, Zigaboo Modeliste (The Meters), The Ray Charles Project, and many more.
​
Flynn's new quartet DUBLINESQUE brings his deep soul and gospel roots together with the Irish music traditions he was raised on.
​
"Dublinesque is my attempt to recreate the kind of parties we had in my parent's house, growing up in Dublin," explains Flynn. "There'd be neighbours and friends and it would always end up as a sing-song/jam session. Everyone would participate - if you couldn't hold a tune you'd perform a 'recitation' or tell a joke!
​
"There was never any delineation between genres of music - whether it was Irish tunes and ballads, soul music or a Beatles song," he emphasizes.
​
The band brings together three talented Bay Area Irish traditional musicians: fellow Irishman Félim Egan (The Black Brothers) on accordion, local favorite Darcy Noonan on fiddle, and from Basque country, Spain, Hector Bragado on banjo. They are also sometimes joined by special guests. Previous guests have included Glide Memorial Choir, Maria Muldaur, Mary Black, Róisín O, Michael Black, Shay Black, Autumn Rhodes, Margaret Graham and dancers from the Kennelly, Dillon and Whelan Schools of Irish Dance and the Cooley-Keegan Branch of Comhaltas Ceoltóirí.
​
"This is my chance to play with some of my favorite musicians and recreate those parties!" says Flynn.
​
Flynn's latest of three solo albums is 'Anywhere But Home,' celebrating Dublin from his San Francisco pandemic perspective. It received praise and widespread airplay in the US, Canada, Europe and Australia.
"Flynn's songwriting moves with true emotional register across history, folklore and poetry…with grit and true Dublin savvy.” Deirdre Cronin - Irish Music Magazine

Students will be creating a single 8x10 still life from start to finish, painting citrus fruit with a blue cup. Students will learn to observe shapes and their relationship to space, utilize tone and color to demonstrate depth, light, and shadow, and how to complete an acrylic painting. This class is perfect for beginners, and painters of all skill-levels, looking to hone in their acrylic painting skills. This class focuses on utilizing eco-friendly materials and uses non-toxic, plastic free Natural Earth Paint, which is safe to wash down your drain without impacting the Earth! About the Teacher: Amy Sundahl is a painter and visual artist. She grew up surrounded by the green hills of Northern California. The palette of blue sky, green and gold hills, grey coastal cliffs, and burnt orange redwoods still inform her work today. Amy began to be influenced by the abstract shapes and large plains of the city scape. These influences show up in structured spaces and textures in her work. To Amy, everyday life is rich in color and meaning. Her approach comes with curiosity and humor. Amy’s work has been compared to American artists such as Edward Hopper, Wayne Thiebaud, and Richard Diebenkorn. Amy currently lives in Long Beach, CA.
